newsitem.title: spain: Spain threatens to issue travel advisory for Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Spain threatens to issue travel advisory for Cuba.

text.p: Spain, angered by the imprisonment of a Spanish tourist in Cuba, threatened on Wednesday to issue a travel advisory and take other measures against the communist island to demand his release.

"This situation is intolerable," Foreign Minister Abel Matutes told state radio. "Spain is going to use all its resources and those of its European partners to get his immediate release and return to Spain."

The row, the latest in a series this year between Cuba and its former colonial power, developed when Spanish tourist Jesus Martin, 30, was arrested and put in prison after a small traffic accident a month ago.

Martin, speaking to state radio from Cuba, said he had been asked to pay for damages and had been imprisoned when he could not immediately come up with the money. He has been held since then without being able to speak to a lawyer or see a judge.

Matutes said the case was strange because the car Martin was driving was insured, there were no injuries and only a small amount of damage. The minister said he thought Martin had been the victim of a ruse to get money.
He said Spain was studying a possible travel advisory warning for Cuba because of its "absolute lack of judicial controls".
"We are studying the possibility, given this lack of guarantees, of recommending that Spanish citizens do not travel to Cuba," he said.
